The titer is consistent: converting the tabulated value with the milli/kilo factor gives5.83[10]g per litre, exactly the figure quoted in the text.The strain names, however, do not match. The table names the engineered strainJNB5–1 → SMCH[11], whereas the text calls it PG. The designation SMCH appears nowhere in the prose, and PG appears only in the text; the sole PG-like name in the table belongs to a different entry, the activator-overexpression strain[12][13], which the text also discusses separately with a different titer[14][15]. So the row is unambiguously identified by strategy, reference, time and titer, but the strain label in the text is inconsistent with the table, and the document gives no note reconciling the names.[16]
